Dry the material at 90� + 5�C to constant mass. Grind and mix well. Transfer the material to a wide-mouthed bottle and stomer it. Do not expose the sample to an atmosphere containing acidic or ~lkaline Use this prepared sample for tests. fumes. A-2.

ASSAY

against a standard solution of diazotized 4-chloroaniline. A-2.1 Reagents A-2.1.1 Hydrochloric Acid -- 30 percent (m/v).
A-2.1.2 Sodium JVitrite Solution -- 10 percent A-2.1.3

Starch Iodide Test Papers

A-2.2

Procedure

Diazonium Salt Solution -- A-2.2.1 Preparation of Standard 4Chloroaniline weigh accurately about 7 g of 4-chloroaniline and dissolve in 25 ml of COOI to OQc in an ice. bath. hydrochloric acid and 100 ml of water. ~iazotize with mechanical stirring -by the addition of sodium nitrite solution from a burette dropwise untd a siight excess of nitrite is shown on the starch iodide paper. The nitrite reaction should be faintly positive even after about 20 minutes. Transfer the clear diazonium solution to a 500-ml volumetric flask and make up the volume with Store this standard solution in an ice-bath in the dark. ice-cold water. 6

IS :8552 -1977 A-2.2.2 Determination of I-( 4'-Sulphophenyl )-3-Carboxyd-Pyrazolone Weigh accurately about 20 g of the prepared sample ( see A-l.1 ), dissolve in 15 ml of sodium hydroxide solution and make up to 500 ml in a volumetric flask. Pipette out 50 ml of the solution into a beaker and d~ilute to about 300 ml with water. Under stirring, add dropwise dilute acetic acid until the PH is 7 as indicated by pH paper. Add to the suspension 200 ml of sodium acetate solution. While stirring mechanically, add the diazonium salt solution from a burette which is provided with a jacket through which ice-cold water is circulated. The burette should be of amber-coloured glass to minimize any decomposition of the diazonium salt by.light. Titrate as rapidly as the s-pot test permits. At the end point of tiration, pyrazolone should be absent and a trace excess of the diazonium salt should be present. To test for excess pyrazolone, place a drop of the titration mixture on a filter paper and bring it into contact w~ith the drop of the 4-chloroaniline diazonium salt solution. A yellow colour developing at the zone of contact of the two solution indicates the presence of pyrazolone. To test for excess diazonium salt use the H acid indicator solution similarly. A pink colour developing at the zone of contact indicates the presence of diazonium salt.
A-2.2.3 It is advantageous to carry out a pilot titration by adding the diazonium standard solution in 1 ml portions to ascertain the approximate range in which the end point lies. Now carry out the accurate titration by adding the diazonium salt solution in 1 ml portions at the beginning, and then in 0.2 ml portions as the end point approaches. Note the volume of the diazonium salt solution required for the titration. A-2.3

A-3. TEST FOR SOLUTION

A-3.1 Procedure - Weigh 1 g of the prepared sample ( see A-l.1 ) Add exactly 10 ml of sodium hydroxide solution to it into _a test-tube. and stir with a glass rod. The material shall dissolve completely at room temperature and shall give a clear yellow coloured solution in order to pass the test.
